persona: A new security-tool user installing the exact published Beta.3 package and scanning an unfamiliar repository.

findings.finding: The zero-argument command scans the current directory, is offline/read-only, and uses concise output. --details, --json and --sarif expose deeper evidence without making the default noisy.

Interactive scan completes with exit 0 even when findings exist; `ci`/`verify` provide threshold exit 1. This is coherent, but the distinction must remain conspicuous so users do not mistake `scan` for a CI policy gate.
UNKNOWN is labeled as not proven secure, carries evidence gaps and limitations, and is explained through details/text and `explain`; it is not rendered as a clean pass.

Findings expose stable rule identity/version, proof, confidence, reachability, evidence anchors, prerequisites, impact and remediation class; terminal control characters and secret values are sanitized/redacted.

Planning is zero-write. Only one exact SAFE transformation may autoapply; non-interactive mutation is withheld without the required intent, REVIEW_REQUIRED/ARCHITECTURAL changes do not autoapply, and verification/rescan outcomes are explicit.

Usage, scan, verification, withheld-remediation and provider failures are separated by exit code. Missing and permission-denied paths fail with actionable path context; malformed analyzable input remains a successful scan with explicit partial coverage.

SARIF 2.1.0 preserves proof and coverage properties, stable fingerprints, supported code flows and exact SAFE fixes. The exact Beta.3 release gate validated it with Microsoft SARIF Multitool and the checksum-pinned official schema.

Setup persists exact Node/entrypoint/version and canonical root rather than an ephemeral package-manager command. Status/verify are readable and MCP exposes exactly three tools. Host UI/version compatibility remains best-effort.
On Windows npm 11.19.1 the exact-version shorthand did not infer the package bin and could fall through to an older global command.
findings.resolution: README and package validation now require the explicit `npm exec --yes --package=... -- cydetix` form for an exact pin.

findings.finding: The Beta.3 baseline documentation recommended older Alpha versions and described Beta.3 as unpublished or unvalidated.
findings.resolution: Public installation, claims, limitations, agent/plugin and release/provenance pages now identify immutable released Beta.3 exactly without exaggerating its assurance.

findings.finding: The Beta.3 documentation did not distinguish stable CLI/report/MCP guarantees from experimental diagnostics and host integration surfaces.
findings.resolution: docs/V1_COMPATIBILITY.md and contract-policy.json now classify every required surface and define its evolution rules.
